claim: The learned treatment now imports authenticated transition evidence across deterministic four-episode generations and uses fitted Q values in generation two. On the sealed eight-seed Ordon workload it improves terminal success from 4/8 to 5/8 at slightly lower native-tick cost without reducing end-to-end throughput, but its best retained route regresses from 130 to 147 ticks. This is evidence that learning is active and currently over-exploits the first successful tactic; it does not satisfy the learning-value or route-quality gates.

bindings.terminal: authenticated F_SP103 to F_SP104 load-zone commit

after.kind: shared authenticated corpus across two deterministic generations

observations.learning_is_active: All generation-two seeds imported 13 globally deduplicated transition rows. Their retained 147-tick terminal tactic carried a fitted mean Q of 98.58 and was selected as greedy or as the explicit greedy control beside an epsilon proposal.
observations.reliability: Shared learning adds one terminal success while charging 74 fewer native ticks.
observations.coverage: The final campaign evaluates 22 distinct tapes and endpoints in 32 proposals, essentially matching the independent treatment's 23 while preserving an exploit control.
observations.route_quality: Every learned generation-two success repeats the first generation's 147-tick terminal tactic. The independent treatment had discovered a 130-tick success, so the critic has not demonstrated cost-sensitive improvement.
observations.throughput: Passing live corpora between generations in memory keeps campaign wall below the independent run despite the model-sharing barrier. This is a 5.4 percent useful-decision throughput increase, not the P1 order-of-magnitude target.

next_engineering_target: Use equal native-tick treatment cells and cost-sensitive successful-tactic exploration so later generations search below the best observed terminal cost instead of repeatedly exploiting the first terminal tactic.
